name: רָם
summary: Three bearers: Ram son of Hezron of Judah, father of Amminadab and so an ancestor of David and of Jesus (Rut 4:19; 1Ch 2:9–10; Mat 1:3–4, Ἀράμ); Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel, Hezron's other son (1Ch 2:25, 27); and the clan of Ram from which Elihu the Buzite came (Job 32:2). The name is the qal participle רָם, “high, exalted”, the word said of Yahweh, “high above all nations” (Psa 113:4); scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Hezron fathered רָם, and Ram fathered Amminadab.”
The sons of Hezron: Jerahmeel, Ram and Chelubai.
In the genealogy of Jesus: “Hezron fathered Aram (Ἀράμ), and Aram fathered Amminadab.”
“The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron: Ram the firstborn …”
“Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram.”
“רָם עַל־כָּל־גּוֹיִם יַהְוֶה”: the word of the name, said of Yahweh.

note: BDB's t.bm.af (16 tokens) also counts the qal participle רָם of the verb wherever it is spelt alike (Deu 8:14; Isa 6:1; Psa 113:4 …), so its count is inflated. Whether Elihu's clan Ram is the same as either man of Judah, scripture does not say; TIPNR keeps three.
